## What's Changed

**NOTE:** This release is a unified release of the NVIDIA Container Toolkit that consists of the following packages:
* [`libnvidia-container 1.20.1`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/libnvidia-container/releases/tag/v1.20.1)
* [`nvidia-container-toolkit 1.20.1`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/releases/tag/v1.20.1)

The packages for this release are published to the [`libnvidia-container` package repositories](https://nvidia.github.io/libnvidia-container/).

### Fixes and Features

- CDI specifications and JIT-CDI mode now inject MIG management capability devices into containers. Set the NVIDIA_MIG_CONFIG_DEVICES or NVIDIA_MIG_MONITOR_DEVICES environment variable to all in a container with CAP_SYS_ADMIN to inject the /dev/nvidia-caps/ device nodes for MIG partition management. For supported values and constraints, refer to [MIG Management Devices](https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/cloud-native/container-toolkit/1.20.1/docker-specialized.html#id2). For more information, refer to [issue #1740](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/issues/1740) and [PR #1947](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/pull/1947).
- Containers can now enforce soft and hard per-GPU CUDA memory limits. Set the NVIDIA_GPU_MEMORY_REQUEST and NVIDIA_GPU_MEMORY_LIMIT environment variables in MiB to control the limits. This feature requires an R615 or later driver. For more information, refer to [PR #2075](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/pull/2075).
- Containers running with an R615 or later driver now receive the GPU firmware files that the driver requires at runtime. CDI specifications include the ucode_*.bin files automatically. For more information, refer to [PR #2095](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/pull/2095).
- The nvidia-ctk runtime configure command now preserves existing Docker feature flags when enabling CDI. Previously, running the command could overwrite flags such as containerd-snapshotter. For more information, refer to [PR #2049](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/pull/2049).
- Fixed an intermittent EBADF error in the create-symlinks hook that caused container creation to fail on busy hosts. The error occurred when the garbage collector closed a file descriptor while a system call was in progress. For more information, refer to [PR #2082](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/pull/2082).
- Fixed a regression in the update-ldcache hook that caused container creation to fail under gVisor. The hook now uses a sealed memfd to execute ldconfig, which avoids mounting /proc inside the container root. For more information, refer to [PR #2059](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/pull/2059).
- On WSL2, setting NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=none now correctly prevents GPU device injection. For more information, refer to [PR #2025](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/pull/2025).
- Fixed NVIDIA X.Org driver module mount paths so that containers render correctly when the host uses a custom ModulePath in xorg.conf.d. For more information, refer to [PR #1980](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/pull/1980).
- GPU devices are now available in the CDI specification on first boot. The nvidia-cdi-refresh systemd service creates NVIDIA control device nodes before generating the specification. For more information, refer to [PR #1979](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/pull/1979).
- GPU containers that start at boot no longer fail due to missing device nodes. The nvidia-cdi-refresh service is now ordered before Docker, containerd, and CRI-O. For more information, refer to [PR #2019](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/pull/2019).
- Containers on read-only filesystems no longer fail to start when the application profile cannot be updated. The update-application-profile hook now ignores read-only filesystem errors. For more information, refer to [PR #2028](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/pull/2028).
- Fixed malformed hook scratch directory names that could prevent hooks from running correctly. For more information, refer to [PR #2042](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/pull/2042).
- Containers running under crun with user namespaces no longer encounter permission errors when resolving the rootfs path. The OCI state parser now uses the non-standard root field from crun. For more information, refer to [PR #1971](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/pull/1971).

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/compare/v1.20.0...v1.20.1

ggml-org/llama.cpp.body: ## Overview This release adds OCP FP8 E4M3 quantization support, a new `flash_attn_ext_rows` op that makes the unified KV cache efficient for multi-sequence inference, and a generic batched tensor copy API. Four new architectures are supported (Clover, Limite, Metis-1.6 and Mistral Large 4), audio generation and transcription expand with Chatterbox TTS, Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and predefined Pocket TTS voices, and the Gemma 4 E2B/E4B models get major prefill optimizations. `ggml` is updated to v0.29.0, bringing FP8 E4M3, flash attention rows, NCCL-based multi-node tensor parallelism and performance work across the CPU, CUDA, SYCL, Metal, Vulkan, OpenCL and Hexagon backends. The server and UI receive a round of fixes and refinements. ### Highlights - Quant: OCP FP8 E4M3 tensor type (saturating mode) with conversion helpers and a new ftype ([#27512](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27512)) - llama: `flash_attn_ext_rows` - more efficient unified KV for multi-seq, restoring non-unified KV prefill performance ([#29510](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29510)) - ggml: batched tensor copy API (`ggml_backend_tensor_copy_n`/`set_n`/`get_n`) superseding the `_2d` API, implemented for Metal and CUDA ([#30881](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30881)) - For a 3rd year in a row, `llama.cpp` is a featured repo in the [Github Octoverse report](https://github.blog/news-insights/octoverse/octoverse-commits-pushes-reach-new-highs-in-2026-as-developers-build-with-agents/): ### API changes - llama.h: add `LLAMA_FTYPE_MOSTLY_F8_E4M3` ([#27512](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27512)) - mtmd.h: add `MTMD_GEN_AUDIO_TYPE_CHATTERBOX` and `n_voices` to `mtmd_gen_audio_info` ([#30993](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30993)) - mtmd.h: add predefined-voice APIs: `mtmd_gen_audio_voice_name()`, `mtmd_gen_audio_get_voice()`, `mtmd_gen_state_set_ref()` ([#30993](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30993)) - mtmd.h: add `mtmd_bitmap_is_voice()` and `mtmd_gen_audio_read_tensor()` ([#30993](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30993)) - mtmd.h: add `MTMD_VIDEO_TEMPLATE_QWEN3VL` video prompt template ([#31619](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31619)) - server: `GET /props` reports the model's predefined TTS `voices`; the TTS endpoint accepts predefined voice names ([#30993](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30993)) - server: `/v1/responses` now merges `extra_params` (seed, min_p, ...) into the converted chat-completions response ([#30959](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30959)) ### New models - Clover-35B-A3B-Preview diffusion model, AR mode ([#31306](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31306)) - Limite 1B - Violetto ([#29433](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29433)) - Metis-1.6 (Praxis ~2.9B and Logos ~10.2B): hybrid Mamba-2 / GQA attention with fixed-depth recurrence and LatentMoE ([#31134](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31134)) - Mistral Large 4 ([#31376](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31376)) ### Core changes - gemma4: graph optimizations with massive prefill gains for E2B and E4B ([#31356](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31356)); create `token_embd` before the tied output in gemma3n and gemma4 ([#31394](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31394)) - LFM3: enable NVFP4 GGUFs ([#31608](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31608)), enable tensor split ([#31431](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31431)), quantize the audio codec decoder ([#31386](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31386)) - spec dec: save and restore MTP hidden state in context checkpoints ([#30141](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30141)) and record LFM3 layer inputs ([#31598](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31598)) - dflash: copy hidden features via device copies ([#31506](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31506)); qwen4exp: write the conv state tail without an intermediate cont ([#31443](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31443)) - model loading: reuse the tensor staging buffer and skip the direct-IO bounce buffer ([#31321](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31321)) - kv-cache: keep Hadamard rotation constants on the GPU ([#31073](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31073)) and fix attention tensor rotation in layers with shared KV ([#31406](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31406)) - kv-cache: never return 0 `kv_rows` for sequences without cells ([#31570](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31570)) and refuse rollbacks past the snapshots of the last ubatch ([#31368](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31368)) - Gemma4 MTP assistant: follow `ctx_other` devices and flash-attention setting ([#31635](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31635)); DSV4: remove simple batch splitting ([#31300](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31300)) - chat: strip the qwen3-coder think block with `reasoning_format none` ([#31380](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31380)) and end reasoning budget forcing on a prompt end tag ([#31374](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31374)) - chat: allow a constraint type after the gpt-oss final channel ([#31556](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31556)); common: fix `-hf` tag matching inside longer quant names ([#31620](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31620)) and bound control vector layer indices ([#31336](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31336)) - tools: reject mismatched shards in GGUF split merge ([#31579](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31579)), fix `imatrix --nextn` crash ([#31522](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31522)), fix `gguf-py` `np_roundf` dropping the sign ([#31310](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31310)) - vendor: miniaudio 0.11.26 ([#31459](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31459)) and cpp-httplib 0.64.0 ([#31400](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31400)); embed an app manifest in all Windows executables ([#31329](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31329)) ### Multi-modality changes - add Chatterbox TTS support ([#30993](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30993)) - add Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe support: offline transcription in 40 languages with prompt context and speaker attribution ([#31471](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31471)) - Pocket TTS: support predefined voices without voice cloning ([#31429](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31429)) - accurate support for the qwen3-vl video prompt format ([#31619](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31619)) - resize Gemma 4 images without letterbox padding ([#30922](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30922)) and fix InternVL CLS token order ([#30886](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30886)) ### Server changes - cap shared decision prefixes at the first output ([#30710](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30710)) - restore the speculative checkpoint for drafts longer than `n_rs_seq` ([#31350](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31350)) ### UI changes - add MCP group checkboxes in the tools settings ([#31303](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31303)) and request persistent storage on startup ([#31299](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31299)) - keep chats at the bottom until the reader scrolls up ([#31311](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31311)) and show the submit button when the input has content ([#31324](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31324)) - reveal the collapsed sidebar from its logo ([#31307](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31307)) and align alert dialog styling ([#31312](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31312)) - keep queued steering messages in their own conversation ([#31304](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31304)) and show an interrupted state for tool calls that never returned ([#31314](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31314)) - disable model deletion the server would refuse ([#31305](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31305)) and prefer a loading model in pre-selection ([#31326](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31326)) - add a Playwright harness for recording demo videos ([#31318](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31318)) and run local browser tests in installed Chrome ([#31596](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31596)) ### ggml changes - [v0.29.0](https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml/releases/tag/v0.29.0): ggml v0.29.0 adds an OCP FP8 E4M3 tensor type, a new `ggml_flash_attn_ext_rows` op where each query slice attends to its own list of K/V rows, a batched tensor copy API, and initial support for multi-node tensor parallelism through a new multi-process communicator interface. Core improvements include bounding tensor views by the bytes their strides reach, zero-copy GGUF export of host-buffer tensors, and `vm_allocate`-based allocations on Apple platforms. Performance work spans all major backends: new SVE kernels in the CPU backend, DPAS flash attention for quantized KV in SYCL, fused MoE MMQ in CUDA, faster MXFP4 mat-vec in Metal, split-K tuning in Vulkan, and a large expansion of quantized GEMM/GEMV coverage in OpenCL. The Hexagon backend gains support for several new ops, including the lightning indexer, top-k mask, conv2d and upscale. ## Assets **Nightly build:** ## 6.73.0 (November 11, 2026)

BREAKING CHANGES:

* resource/aws_wafv2_web_acl_rule: Removes `and_statement` from `statement` blocks nested in `and_statement`, and `or_statement` from `statement` blocks nested in `or_statement`. These values are rejected by AWS. ([#50604](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws/issues/50604))
* resource/aws_wafv2_web_acl_rule: Removes `managed_rule_group_statement`, `rate_based_statement` and `rule_group_reference_statement` from `statement` blocks nested in `and_statement`, `not_statement` and `or_statement`. These values are rejected by AWS. ([#50604](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws/issues/50604))
* resource/aws_wafv2_web_acl_rule: Removes `or_statement` from `statement` blocks nested in `or_statement`. These values are rejected by AWS. ([#50604](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws/issues/50604))

NOTES:

* resource/aws_efs_file_system: Until AWS roll out the service change supporting the new default encryption setting, changing `encrypted = true` to `encrypted = false` will seem to have succeeded without modifying anything on the AWS side. In this scenario you will need to manually recreate the file system via `terraform destroy` and `terraform apply` ([#49999](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws/issues/49999))

## Summary

This release updates the default lychee version from `v0.23.0` to `v0.24.2`.

The main reason for this release is compatibility with the new lychee `0.24.x` release artifacts. Starting with lychee `v0.24.0`, the archive layout changed, and the `lychee` binary may now be packaged inside a subdirectory. `lychee-action` now detects that layout automatically, so users can upgrade without changing their workflows.

If you use:

```yaml
uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2
```

you will get the new version once the floating `v2` tag has been updated. If you pin exact versions, update to:

```yaml
uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2.9.0
```

## What’s new from lychee `v0.24.x`

### Better diagnostics

lychee now reports line and column numbers for detected links. This makes broken link reports easier to act on, especially in larger documentation sites or generated reports.

### Text fragment checking

lychee can now check URL text fragments, such as links containing `#:~:text=...`. This helps catch links that point to a valid page but no longer points to the intended highlighted text.

### Sitemap support

lychee can now read `sitemap.xml` inputs. This is useful for checking published websites or generated documentation sites where the sitemap is the easiest source of URLs to validate.

### JUnit output

lychee now supports JUnit output. This makes it easier to integrate link checking results with CI systems and test reporting tools that understand JUnit XML.

### Redirect and remap visibility

lychee can now show redirects and remaps more clearly. This helps explain why a URL was checked as a different final URL and makes debugging link-checking behavior easier.

### Multiple config files

lychee now supports multiple configuration files and expanded config handling. This is useful for repositories that split documentation, website, or package-specific link-checking settings.

### Timeout handling

lychee can now accept timeouts explicitly. This gives users more control over how strict their link checks should be for flaky or slow endpoints.

## Fixes and reliability improvements

### Fixed lychee `0.24.x` archive compatibility

`lychee-action` now handles the new lychee release archive layout by detecting whether the `lychee` binary is inside a subdirectory.

This fixes compatibility with lychee `0.24.x`.

### More stable installation path

The action now installs lychee into `$RUNNER_TEMP/lychee/bin` instead of `$HOME`.

This avoids failures on runners where `$HOME` differs between composite action steps. In those environments, the action could add one directory to `PATH` but install the binary somewhere else, causing `lychee: command not found`.

### Safer automatic lychee version updates

The workflow that checks for new lychee releases now guards against `null` release versions before creating update PRs. This prevents invalid automated PRs such as “Update lycheeVersion to null”.

### Dependency updates

- Updated `actions/checkout` from `v6` to `v7`
- Updated `actions/cache` from `v5` to `v6`

## Upstream lychee changelog

For the full lychee changelog, see:

- https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/releases/tag/lychee-v0.24.0
- https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/releases/tag/lychee-v0.24.1
- https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/releases/tag/lychee-v0.24.2

## What’s Changed

* bump default to 0.24.1 and auto-detect lychee bin in subfolder by @kaitlyndotmoe in https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee-action/pull/330
* fixes #322 check for null by @bgermann in https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee-action/pull/336
* Install into `$RUNNER_TEMP` instead of `$HOME` by @mre in https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee-action/pull/338
* Bump actions/checkout from 6 to 7 by @dependabot in https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee-action/pull/339
* Bump actions/cache from 5 to 6 by @dependabot in https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee-action/pull/340
